fichas.title: Responsibilities of Historic Building Authorities
fichas.summary: Outlines the division of responsibilities between higher and lower historic building authorities. Tasks include research, documentation, monument evaluation, consultation, approval, subsidies, implementation, monitoring, and care or protection of monuments; responsibilities may vary by state.
uses: Conservation and alteration of historic buildings
Consultation and approval of refurbishment work
Implementation and monitoring of protection measures
figure_refs: Figure 1: Principles of the division of responsibilities regarding listed building protection and care of historic buildings

fichas.title: Types of Listed Building Protection
fichas.summary: Explains the effects of protection for an individual listed building, a conservation area or ensemble, and a preservation by-law. Individual listing protects structure and appearance and requires approval for alterations or interventions. Area-based protection generally concerns external appearance or planning considerations. Early consultation with responsible authorities is recommended.
spaces: Area subject to a preservation by-law
uses: Protecting the character and appearance of buildings or areas
figure_refs: Figure 2: Difference and effects of various legal protection measures

fichas.title: Legal Consequences of Statutory Lists of Historic Buildings
fichas.summary: Compares constitutive and declarative systems for listing historic buildings. In the constitutive system, formal entry is the basis for applying historic-building law and the owner must be informed. In the declarative system, listing serves scientific information and has no legal consequences; listing status may be obtained by enquiry to the responsible authority.
uses: Determining the legal effect of listing
figure_refs: Figure 3: Legal consequences of the types of statutory lists of historic buildings

fichas.title: Protection of Existing Use
fichas.summary: Describes the principle that existing uses may remain protected when they would not be approvable under current regulations but were formerly approved or suitable for approval. Maintenance and modernization are possible if the building's identity is preserved. A change of use, replacement of building structure, or other alterations requiring approval can end this protection and trigger the need to meet modern standards. Early discussion with the responsible authority is advised.
uses: Modernising an existing building while preserving its identity
Assessing whether existing-use protection applies before alteration or change of use
